passages.title: Internship agencies
content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 3: "Internship agencies"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [00:52] Danny: Hi, Sarah.
[00:55] Sarah: Oh, hi, Danny.
[00:56] Danny: I was thinking, when I finish my degree, I'd like to do a short work placement with a company to get some experience.
[01:03] Sarah: Oh, an internship you mean?

[01:05] Danny: Yeah. If I'm applying for a job in the future, after my placement, then the company would say, OK, this guy is organised and can clearly think ahead and decide what he wants to do, and that could give me an advantage over other candidates for the same job, even if they've got more experience than me in other areas.
[01:25] Sarah: Well, maybe. You interested in an internship?
[01:29] Danny: Definitely, but it'd have to be with a huge corporation.
[01:32] Sarah: Right. Why?
[01:33] Danny: Because they tend to be multinational, possibly with openings for interns in offices across the globe, so I could choose where to go rather than staying in the UK.
[01:44] Sarah: But wouldn't you just end up working with people you never see again?
[01:48] Danny: Maybe, but internships aren't only about networking, are they?
[01:52] Sarah: True.
[01:53] Danny: I was glad when our tutor told us about some of the agencies that can arrange internships for us.
[01:58] Sarah: Yes, but there are so many that it might be hard to choose one, especially because most work in all sectors rather than specialising in a specific field.
[02:07] Danny: Exactly, and most just say exactly the same on their websites.
[02:11] Sarah: Right. Hard to tell them apart.
[02:14] Danny: So, I reckon the way to go is to reach out to someone who arranged a placement through them?
[02:19] Sarah: Right, and ask them what the agency was really like.
[02:22] Danny: Exactly.
[02:23] Sarah: The tutor said she can help put us in touch with some recent graduates for that.
[02:26] Danny: Sure. Having said that, my cousin, right, she qualified as an accountant and then got a placement in a construction company in the Middle East.
[02:35] Sarah: Doing accounting, presumably?
[02:37] Danny: Yeah. The thing is, though, she didn't bother registering with any agencies. She just went straight to the HR people in the firm and asked for a placement with them.
[02:46] Sarah: A speculative application, then.
[02:48] Danny: Yeah.
[02:49] Sarah: Did it work?
[02:50] Danny: Yeah, she got one. So, I might just do what she did.
[02:53] Sarah: Right. Another option is a remote internship.
[02:58] Danny: What, an online internship? Where you never actually go into the office?
[03:02] Sarah: That's right. So you could do it one day a week, while doing your degree.
[03:06] Danny: But if you never meet your colleagues or enter a work environment, I can't see the purpose of a remote internship.

[03:14] Sarah: Actually, I think you're missing the point. Could be a great way to test it for a while, you know, working with a company. And once the initial internship is over, then, if you're happy with the company, you could go on to a face-to-face internship with them as the next step.
[03:28] Danny: Well, I suppose that's true. I think it would be useful to review what the tutor said about the various internship agencies.
[04:20] Sarah: Yes, they've all got their unique selling points.
[04:23] Danny: Sure.
[04:23] Sarah: Let's start with Interntastic.
[04:26] Danny: Weren't they the ones who pride themselves on sorting out the practicalities before the internship starts?
[04:32] Sarah: Yes, even the airport transfer if you move somewhere. So the intern doesn't have to lift a finger until it starts.
[04:39] Danny: Yeah. And Total Internships, the one whose fees aren't as high as most of the other agencies.
[04:46] Sarah: Oh, yes. The tutor did say, though, that we should expect to pay a substantial sum for a decent placement to be arranged.
[04:53] Danny: Hmm. So perhaps Total Internships don't provide such a high standard of service.
[04:59] Sarah: And they don't seem to have such a strong reputation either.
[05:02] Danny: You may be right there.
[05:04] Sarah: Unlike IMC Group, they're really highly thought of, aren't they?
[05:07] Danny: Definitely. Seem to be head and shoulders above the rest.
[05:12] Sarah: Quite pricey, though.
[05:13] Danny: Well, hopefully you get what you pay for with them. What about Interns International?
[05:19] Sarah: Well, while the other organisations are vague about whether we'd get paid or not, these guys make it a policy that interns are not just there to provide free labour.
[05:29] Danny: Right.
[05:29] Sarah: Interns that go through Interns International might not necessarily get a salary as such, but if they don't, then they'd get a living allowance while they're working.
[05:39] Danny: That's the deal.
[05:40] Sarah: Yes.
[05:40] Danny: I'm not sure what the distinction is.
[05:43] Sarah: Something with tax laws, maybe?
[05:45] Danny: Possibly.
[05:47] Sarah: And Placements.com. They pride themselves on getting to know every individual who wants to find an internship, don't they?
[05:54] Danny: Yes. Matching them up with the internship they're most compatible with.
[05:58] Sarah: And being really thorough about it.
[06:00] Danny: Yeah.
[06:01] Sarah: That's what they say.

explanation.step3: Tổ chức Interns International có đặc điểm gì nổi bật? → Các đáp án có những từ như: paid , living allowance , free labour , nên học viên cần chú ý đến thông tin về tiền lương hoặc hỗ trợ tài chính . ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : 00:05:17 → 00:05:39 Sarah: “...these guys make it a policy that interns are not just there to provide free labour. ” Sarah: “They might not necessarily get a salary , but if they don’t, then they’ll get a living allowance while working.” ☺️ Giải thích : Sarah nói rõ rằng Interns International có chính sách đảm bảo thực tập sinh không làm không công Họ có thể không nhận lương (salary) , nhưng nếu không có lương thì sẽ được nhận trợ cấp sinh hoạt (living allowance) → Điều này cho thấy đặc điểm nổi bật của họ là: bảo đảm thực tậ
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: They ensure that all interns are paid.

passages.title: Passive homes on farms
content: 📌 Passive homes on farms
passive buildings = those which are designed to use very little energy
Coombs Farm
The clients had always lived in old farmhouses which were cold, [ _____ ] and dark.
They eventually got permission to build a house without a [ _____ ]
The building's appearance is traditional, e.g. the roof is made from [ _____ ]
Modern technology was used, e.g. triple-glazing and solar thermal panels.
The building is designed to handle [ _____ ] on site.
Ballcross Farmhouse
Many of the building materials were effectively free and have a low impact, including:
500 tonnes of [ _____ ]the [ _____ ] which were already on the land [ _____ ] which was used inside the building  which was turned into insulation
Edensor Farm
The building features a central [ _____ ]
The design works so well that the building:
only needs one [ _____ ]doesn't use any [ _____ ]has an extremely low carbon footprint
transcript: [01:15] AUDIO: Welcome to today's lecture in which I'd like to focus on buildings which achieve extremely high standards of energy efficiency through their design, especially with regard to heating or cooling. Now the buildings I'd like to tell you about today are all farmhouses. The first of these passive homes is Coombs Farm, built for a couple who'd spent much of their life living in buildings on farms which were often hundreds of years old. But these were very difficult to heat and keep warm.

[01:48] AUDIO: They tended to be damp, plus the tiny windows meant that light levels were low. So they wanted a new build which would be completely different. When they engaged an architect to build them a new eco-house, she had to work around the very strict planning laws that were in place in the region. One of these stated that any new building needed to include a chimney.

[02:10] AUDIO: But as the house was designed with a heat pump, this was unnecessary. And the planners agreed in the end not to insist on this, which saved a substantial amount of money. The building is a mix of ancient and modern technologies. So for example, the roof, like many period buildings in the region, is built of slate, giving it quite a conventional look.

[02:34] AUDIO: But then the windows are triple glazed to the highest specifications, minimizing heat loss. And the building also features solar thermal panels, helping to make it largely self-sufficient in terms of energy. And rather than send the sewage off down the mains to be disposed of, and possibly ending up being dumped in the local river, the owners were keen for it to be dealt with in a compost tank right by the house. And the idea is that it will ultimately be used as fertilizer for the garden.

[03:06] AUDIO: The next farmhouse I'm going to discuss is called Ballcross. And this case study illustrates how farm owners are often well placed to take advantage of the resources available on their land, which has the double advantage of and reducing the environmental impact of the building process. This was certainly the case at Ballcross. There were rocks across the owner's land, absolutely loads of them, something like 500 tons were collected in total.

[03:37] AUDIO: And these were used to construct the external walls of the new farmhouse. Obviously doing that was inexpensive, and it was carbon neutral. Internally, the stairs, floors, and various other components were constructed from the oak which was sourced from around the farm, again effectively at zero cost. The owners are sheep farmers, and so to insulate the walls, roof, and floors, perhaps unsurprisingly, they turned to the wool from their own livestock.

[04:08] AUDIO: It did need to undergo some processing before being usable as an insulating material, but again, it was readily available, virtually free, and of course, completely renewable. And finally, there's Edenzer Farm. This house is designed around a courtyard, which forms the heart of the building, and the windows are carefully aligned with the sun to try and get solar heat gain to a maximum. And it's a really effective system, so much so that the entire house is heated by a single radiator, which is remarkable when you think about it.

[04:46] AUDIO: All the energy is sustainably sourced, with a large array of photovoltaic panels on the roof that generate much of the electricity used in and by the house. And no gas whatsoever is needed by the building, enabling it to achieve a very low carbon footprint. So going forward, it is high-performing buildings like these which are driving the move towards decarbonization, and there's no doubt that once you guys are starting your careers...

questions.prompt: The clients had always lived in old farmhouses which were cold, _____ and dark.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "But these were very difficult to heat and keep warm. They tended to be damp, plus the tiny windows meant that light levels were low."
explanation.step3: Tính từ – vì đứng giữa hai tính từ khác là cold và dark , nên chỗ trống cần một tính từ miêu tả tiêu cực nữa để mô tả điều kiện sống của những căn nhà cũ. ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : 00:01:44 → 00:01:48 “But these were very difficult to heat and keep warm. They tended to be damp , plus the tiny windows meant that light levels were low.” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : Câu trước mô tả nhà cũ “khó giữ ấm”, rồi tiếp theo nói rằng chúng thường ẩm ướt (damp) Đây là từ được dùng để mô tả tình trạng chung của các căn nhà cũ (giống như cold và dark ) Vậy “ damp ” chính là tính từ còn thiếu cần điền. ✅ Đáp án đúng: damp 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ wet => Đây là từ gần nghĩa nhưng mang tính miêu tả cụ thể hơn là tình trạng chung – không phù hợp với “cold” và

questions.prompt: They eventually got permission to build a house without a _____

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "One of these stated that any new building needed to include a chimney. But as the house was designed with a heat pump, this was unnecessary."
explanation.step3: Danh từ đếm được số ít – đứng sau mạo từ “a”, biểu thị một bộ phận kiến trúc cụ thể trong ngôi nhà mà ban đầu bắt buộc phải có. ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : 00:02:06 → 00:02:14 “One of these [planning laws] stated that any new building needed to include a chimney .” “But as the house was designed with a heat pump, this was unnecessary.” “And the planners agreed… not to insist on this…” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : Luật xây dựng yêu cầu ngôi nhà mới phải có một cái gì đó Cụ thể là chimney – ống khói Tuy nhiên, do nhà có heat pump nên không cần ống khói → và được chấp thuận xây không có chimney → Vậy từ bị bỏ trống chính là chimney ✅ Đáp án đúng: chimney 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ fireplace => Từ này thường gắn với nội thất bên trong, không đúng vớ

questions.prompt: The building's appearance is traditional, e.g. the roof is made from _____

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "So for example, the roof, like many period buildings in the region, is built of slate, giving it quite a conventional look."
explanation.step3: Danh từ không đếm được – cần điền tên một loại vật liệu dùng để làm mái nhà. ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : 00:02:25 → 00:02:34 “So for example, the roof, like many period buildings in the region, is built of slate , giving it quite a conventional look.” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : Người nói đang mô tả mái nhà của Coombs Farm Câu này nêu rõ vật liệu dùng là slate – đá phiến Đây là loại vật liệu truyền thống phổ biến, giúp giữ lại vẻ ngoài cổ điển của ngôi nhà → Vậy từ cần điền chính là slate ✅ Đáp án đúng: slate 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ stone => Không đúng: “stone” là nguyên liệu xây tường , không phải mái nhà ❌ tile => Không chính xác: tile là ngói – không phải loại được dùng ở đây. Từ “slate” cụ thể và chính xác hơn.

questions.prompt: The building is designed to handle _____ on site.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "And rather than send the sewage off down the mains to be disposed of, and possibly ending up being dumped in the local river, the owners were keen for it to be dealt with in a compost tank right by the house. And the idea is that it will ultimately be used as fertilizer for the garden."
explanation.step3: Danh từ không đếm được – đề cập đến một loại chất thải sinh hoạt , vì được đặt trong cụm “handle … on site”. ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : 00:02:48 → 00:03:05 “Rather than send the sewage off down the mains to be disposed of... the owners were keen for it to be dealt with in a compost tank…” “The idea is that it will ultimately be used as fertilizer for the garden.” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : Câu hỏi yêu cầu điền thứ gì được xử lý ngay tại chỗ (on site) Trong bài nghe, người nói mô tả chất thải (sewage) không được đưa ra hệ thống cống mà xử lý tại nhà bằng bể ủ phân compost → Như vậy, sewage là từ chính xác cần điền ✅ Đáp án đúng: sewage 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ waste => Tuy gần nghĩa, nhưng “waste” quá chung chung → không mô tả chính xác loại

questions.prompt: 500 tonnes of _____the _____ which were already on the land _____ which was used inside the building  which was turned into insulation

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "There were rocks across the owner's land, absolutely loads of them, something like 500 tons were collected in total."
explanation.step3: Danh từ đếm được số nhiều – vì nằm sau số lượng “500 tonnes of …” nên chắc chắn là một loại vật liệu dạng khối lượng lớn , tự nhiên. ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : 00:03:29 → 00:03:37 “There were rocks across the owner’s land, absolutely loads of them, something like 500 tons were collected in total.” “And these were used to construct the external walls…” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : Người nói kể rằng trên mảnh đất có rất nhiều rocks (đá) Họ thu được khoảng 500 tấn và sử dụng để xây tường ngoài của trang trại → Vậy từ cần điền chính xác là rocks ✅ Đáp án đúng: rocks 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ stones => Mặc dù cũng là đá, nhưng từ trong bài nghe dùng là rocks → từ này phù hợp hơn vì nó mang nghĩa “đá lớn, khối đá xây dựng” ❌ bricks => Không đúng: br

questions.prompt: The building features a central _____

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Internally, the stairs, floors, and various other components were constructed from the oak which was sourced from around the farm, again effectively at zero cost."
explanation.step3: Danh từ không đếm được – vì đứng sau mạo từ “the” và là tên một loại gỗ được dùng bên trong tòa nhà. ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : 00:03:47 → 00:03:58 “Internally, the stairs, floors, and various other components were constructed from the oak , which was sourced from around the farm…” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : Trong nội thất của trang trại Ballcross, họ sử dụng gỗ để làm cầu thang, sàn, và nhiều bộ phận khác Gỗ đó là oak (gỗ sồi), được lấy trực tiếp từ nông trại → Oak chính là vật liệu có sẵn và miễn phí , đúng yêu cầu của câu hỏi ✅ Đáp án đúng: oak 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ wood => “wood” quá chung chung – trong khi audio nói rõ là oak , và IELTS cần câu trả lời chính xác nhất ❌ timber => Tuy cũng nghĩa là gỗ xây dựng, nhưng không phải là từ

questions.prompt: only needs one _____doesn't use any _____has an extremely low carbon footprint

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "It did need to undergo some processing before being usable as an insulating material, but again, it was readily available, virtually free, and of course, completely renewable."
explanation.step3: Danh từ không đếm được – cần điền tên một loại vật liệu cách nhiệt (insulation), được làm từ tài nguyên tại nông trại. ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : 00:04:08 → 00:04:20 “...they turned to the wool from their own livestock.” “It did need to undergo some processing before being usable as an insulating material …” “...readily available, virtually free, and of course, completely renewable.” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : Chủ nông trại nuôi cừu, nên họ tận dụng wool (lông cừu) Đây là vật liệu được dùng để cách nhiệt cho tường, mái và sàn → Từ cần điền chính là wool ✅ Đáp án đúng: wool 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ fur => Fur thường dùng cho lông thú (để mặc) – không dùng làm vật liệu cách nhiệt ❌ fleece => Dù có liên quan đến lông cừu, nhưng trong bài chỉ d

questions.prompt: Ballcross Farmhouse

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "This house is designed around a courtyard, which forms the heart of the building, and the windows are carefully aligned with the sun to try and get solar heat gain to a maximum."
explanation.step3: Danh từ đếm được số ít – mô tả kết cấu trung tâm của tòa nhà, là một phần trong thiết kế tổng thể. ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : 00:04:25 → 00:04:31 “This house is designed around a courtyard , which forms the heart of the building…” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : Câu này cho biết trung tâm (the heart) của tòa nhà là một courtyard – sân trong Kiến trúc này cho phép lấy ánh sáng và nhiệt tự nhiên hiệu quả , giúp tiết kiệm năng lượng → Vậy từ cần điền chính là courtyard ✅ Đáp án đúng: courtyard 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ garden => Không chính xác: garden thường ở ngoài nhà , không phải trung tâm của công trình kiến trúc ❌ patio => Mặc dù gần nghĩa, nhưng “patio” nhỏ hơn và thường không dùng để mô tả trung tâm của một tòa nhà

questions.prompt: Many of the building materials were effectively free and have a low impact, including:

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "And it's a really effective system, so much so that the entire house is heated by a single radiator, which is remarkable when you think about it."
explanation.step3: Danh từ đếm được số ít – cần điền tên một thiết bị sưởi mà toàn bộ ngôi nhà chỉ cần duy nhất một cái . ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : 00:04:36 → 00:04:45 “...the entire house is heated by a single radiator , which is remarkable when you think about it.” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : Người nói nhấn mạnh rằng cả ngôi nhà chỉ dùng một thiết bị sưởi duy nhất Từ khóa rõ ràng là radiator – bộ tản nhiệt → Đây là từ cần điền chính xác ✅ Đáp án đúng: radiator 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ heater => Không sai hoàn toàn, nhưng không phải từ được dùng trong bài nghe – IELTS yêu cầu dùng đúng từ trong audio ❌ boiler => Là nồi hơi – thiết bị khác hoàn toàn và không phù hợp ở đây

questions.prompt: 500 tonnes of _____the _____ which were already on the land _____ which was used inside the building  which was turned into insulation

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "And no gas whatsoever is needed by the building, enabling it to achieve a very low carbon footprint."
explanation.step3: Danh từ không đếm được – cần điền tên một loại nhiên liệu mà ngôi nhà không cần dùng đến. ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : 00:04:57 → 00:05:04 “ And no gas whatsoever is needed by the building , enabling it to achieve a very low carbon footprint.” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : Người nói khẳng định rõ ràng: ngôi nhà không cần dùng đến gas Cụm “no gas whatsoever” = hoàn toàn không cần gas → Đây là yếu tố then chốt giúp tòa nhà có lượng khí thải carbon thấp ✅ Đáp án đúng: gas 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ electricity => Sai hoàn toàn: nhà này có dùng điện , thậm chí còn có hệ thống solar panels tạo ra điện ❌ oil => Không được nhắc đến trong bài nghe – không liên quan đến nội dung câu hỏi

transcript: [00:02] AUDIO: Look at part one. You will hear a woman phoning an estate agent to ask about flats for rent. First you have some time to look at questions one to six. Now listen carefully and answer questions one to six.
[00:53] JAMES LANSMAN: Hello, Colvin Lettings, James Lansman speaking. How can I help?
[00:57] MISS RUSSELL: Oh, hello. I'm just calling to see what flats you currently have available to rent.
[01:03] JAMES LANSMAN: Certainly, madam. What sort of place are you looking for?
[01:06] MISS RUSSELL: Well, a two-bed flat is what I'm really aiming for, but I'm open to other possibilities.
[01:11] JAMES LANSMAN: Of course. Well, we'll see what we can do. What area are you thinking of?
[01:16] MISS RUSSELL: Either in the east side or the old port. I work in the centre, you see, but obviously, I don't really want to live in the centre. Who would?
[01:25] JAMES LANSMAN: I see. When are you thinking of moving?
[01:28] MISS RUSSELL: It would need to be sometime before the 13th of September, as that's when the contract on my old place runs out.
[01:35] JAMES LANSMAN: So before the end of September, then?
[01:38] MISS RUSSELL: No, the middle of September. The 13th.
[01:41] JAMES LANSMAN: Oh, right. Sorry. I thought you said the 30th. And do you have a set amount that you'd be willing to spend?

passages.title: Recycling centres in Bookwall
content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 2: "Recycling centres in Bookwall"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [00:01] AUDIO: Now look at part two. You will hear a man speaking on the radio about recycling in a town called Bookwall. First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 15. Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 15.

[00:48] Radio Bookwall: As our listeners know, on Radio Bookwall we like to focus on sustainable living and today I'm joined in the studio by Kevin, Head of Recycling at Bookwall Council. Welcome Kevin.
[01:00] Kevin: Hi, good to be here.
[01:02] Radio Bookwall: So Kevin, how good are we at recycling our waste here in Bookwall?

[01:08] Kevin: Well, in the years I've been involved in recycling with Bookwall Council, the proportion of waste that's recycled has doubled. We now recycle about 50% of our rubbish and that's a real achievement that I'm proud of. But listeners might be surprised to learn that some countries manage far more than this. And of course, recycling's important in so many ways.

[01:38] Kevin: Take aluminium cans for example. Okay, maybe the drinks inside them aren't super healthy, but the point is that, like lots of packaging, cans can easily be recycled, which is a far more energy efficient process than manufacturing a new can would be. That's a huge benefit, as well as the fact that reusing that aluminium conserves resources. And you know, in the UK we throw away about 26 million tonnes of waste each year.

[02:16] Kevin: To put that into perspective, that's equivalent to the weight of 260 ships, and I mean the large ones that cruise across the seas. That's an enormous amount, and the more of that we can recycle, the better for the environment. We're keen to get the schoolchildren of Bookwall passionate about recycling this year. I did have the idea of a competition for kids to make something out of the items in their recycling, until someone pointed out that this might prevent the things from being recycled.

[02:55] Kevin: So instead, we're asking kids to submit pictures taken of them or their family actually doing their recycling. I'm hoping it'll be even more popular than last year's story-writing competition on the theme of recycling. Bookwall, of course, has several recycling centres across various locations throughout the city, so wherever you live, you're not far from your nearest one, and recyclers may be pleased to learn that we've just extended their opening hours, so now you'll even be able to go after you've finished work.
[03:40] AUDIO: Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 16 to 20. Now listen carefully and answer questions 16 to 20.
[04:20] Radio Bookwall: So, Kevin, can people take anything to the recycling centres in Bookwall?

[04:25] Kevin: I'm glad you asked me. It depends. Let's start with batteries. Now, there are many different types, from the little ones that go into our car keys, and small disposable ones, right through to vehicle batteries.

[04:42] Kevin: At the moment, not all our recycling centres can take every kind, so the best advice is to enquire ahead, phone if in doubt, and explain exactly what type of battery you have, and our staff will be able to advise. It's better to do that than bring something in but then find that we can't accept it. What else? Clothes.

[05:06] Kevin: If there's anything you don't wear anymore or you've outgrown it, we'd love to accept it, so you can just turn up whenever you want at one of our centres. Clothing can often be redistributed to those who need it, which is great. Building materials. You can dispose of these if it's your own small-scale renovation project, but to do this, we ask you to reserve a slot at the recycling centre with a couple of days' notice if you can, please.

[05:39] Kevin: But this service excludes professional builders, I'm afraid. Tradespeople will need to make their own arrangements or hire a skip. Most of our sites can accept furniture, but this is a bit more complicated. Some of our smaller centres can't accept larger items, such as beds, so it's worth having a look on the website in advance.

[06:04] Kevin: It tells you exactly what can be recycled and where, so you can potentially save yourselves a wasted trip. Goods such as laptops, phones and TVs generally have plenty of components that can be salvaged, so you can deposit these at all of our sites. So, feel free to just turn up and drop them off. No need to book an appointment.
[06:31] Kevin: We'd just ask you to make sure you put them in the right skip once you're there.
[06:38] AUDIO: That is the end of part two. You now have some time to check your answers.

explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "We now recycle about 50% of our rubbish and that's a real achievement that I'm proud of."

questions.prompt: What point is Kevin making when he talks about drinks cans?

Recycling an item uses less energy than making a new one would.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Take aluminium cans for example. Okay, maybe the drinks inside them aren't super healthy, but the point is that, like lots of packaging, cans can easily be recycled, which is a far more energy efficient process than manufacturing a new can would be."
explanation.step3: Câu hỏi yêu cầu mình xác định ý chính Kevin muốn nói khi đề cập đến lon nước (drinks cans) . → Các đáp án đều là ý kiến liên quan đến việc tái chế và lon nước , nên cần chú ý đến cụm từ “drinks cans”. ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : 00:01:38 – “Take aluminium cans for example…” ☺️ Giải thích : Kevin nói: “cans can easily be recycled, which is a far more energy efficient process than manufacturing a new can would be.” Điều này trùng khớp chính xác với đáp án B – việc tái chế tiết kiệm năng lượng hơn việc sản xuất mới. ✅ Đáp án đúng: B – Recycling an item uses less energy than making a new one would. 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ A – Kevin có nhắc đến việc đồ uống bên trong không tốt cho sức khỏe, nhưng KHÔNG khuyên tránh mua. ❌ C – Không nói về việc kiểm tra
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: Recycling an item uses less energy than making a new one would.

questions.prompt: Kevin mentions ships in order to
options: explain how much waste is produced.
warn how dangerous rubbish in the sea can be.
point out that a lot of the UK’s rubbish is sent overseas.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "And you know, in the UK we throw away about 26 million tonnes of waste each year. To put that into perspective, that's equivalent to the weight of 260 ships, and I mean the large ones that cruise across the seas. That's an enormous amount, and the more of that we can recycle, the better for the environment."
explanation.step3: Câu hỏi hỏi mục đích của việc Kevin nhắc đến “ships” – tàu thuyền. → Mình cần xác định liệu đó là để giải thích lượng rác , cảnh báo về nguy hiểm , hay nói về xuất khẩu rác . ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : 00:02:08 – “in the UK we throw away about 26 million tonnes of waste each year…” ☺️ Giải thích : Kevin nói: “that’s equivalent to the weight of 260 ships…” → Anh ấy dùng hình ảnh “ships” để giải thích cho người nghe hiểu rõ hơn về lượng rác khổng lồ . ✅ Đáp án đúng: A – explain how much waste is produced. 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ B – Kevin không nói gì về sự nguy hiểm của rác trên biển. ❌ C – Không đề cập đến việc rác bị gửi ra nước ngoài.
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: explain how much waste is produced.

passages.title: Sunrise Lake
content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 3: "Sunrise Lake"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [00:00] AUDIO: Now look at part three. You will hear two literature students preparing for a seminar about a book called Sunrise Lake by the novelist Joyce Clare. First you have some time to look at questions 21 to 26. Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 26.
[00:56] RACHEL: Hi Owen, shall we do our preparation for tomorrow's seminar?
[01:00] OWEN: Hi Rachel, sure. So had you read Sunrise Lake before?
[01:04] RACHEL: No, but I've always been a big fan of Joyce Clare's other books.
[01:09] OWEN: Some were made into films, weren't they?

[01:11] RACHEL: Yes, but not Sunrise Lake for some reason, which is odd because it was hugely popular and it would have made a great movie. Plus, it was the book which made her a big name. No one had heard of her before Sunrise Lake was published.
[01:27] OWEN: Right, I can see why it was a big hit though. I mean, it's an incredibly accomplished piece of writing.
[01:33] RACHEL: Yeah, but when it came out in 1961, the literary critics were very lukewarm in their reviews.
[01:40] OWEN: How bizarre.
[01:41] RACHEL: I suppose Joyce Clare's publishers should take some credit for the book's success. They worked really hard to promote it, placing adverts in the newspapers and doing radio interviews.
[01:52] OWEN: Right, making sure people had heard of it.
[01:54] RACHEL: Exactly.
[01:56] OWEN: Okay, so what should we tell the other students about in the seminar?
[02:00] RACHEL: I wondered about saying what other novels Sunrise Lake is similar to, but I was struggling to come up with any because it's unique really.
[02:09] OWEN: We'll certainly need to explain the plot.
[02:11] RACHEL: Yes, at least summarize the key events that involved the central characters.
[02:16] OWEN: I think the primary thing to focus on is our reactions to the book, especially the heroine and her immediate circle.
[02:23] RACHEL: And our responses to the people she meets.
[02:26] OWEN: Exactly. And the other students may decide they'd like to read the book or not.
[02:32] RACHEL: Which is fine. I mean, the idea isn't to try and sell the book in any way.
[02:37] OWEN: No, that's right.
[02:39] RACHEL: So to get a decent grade, what do we need to do? We've got to run this discussion for what, 15 minutes?
[02:45] OWEN: More or less 15, but we've got flexibility. Doesn't really matter if we go over that, especially if the tutor or the other students ask us lots of questions.

[02:54] RACHEL: Well, you know me, I usually like to prepare slides that look really professional. But as we haven't been asked to do that for this presentation, we'll have to come up with another way of getting a high mark.
[03:05] OWEN: The assessment handbook says something about finding lines of dialogue from books and using these to sort of explain the character's predicament.
[03:15] RACHEL: Right. So we need to find extracts that give us insights into what they're thinking.

[03:20] OWEN: Yeah. And another thing we'll be graded on is applying the themes of the book to the present day, looking at whether the situation of the characters back in 1960 still has anything to say to our generation.
[03:32] RACHEL: Oh, right. Yeah. We'll have to make sure we do that then.
[03:39] AUDIO: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 27 to 30. Now listen carefully and answer questions 27 to 30.
[04:19] RACHEL: So we'll need to present the four main female characters.
[04:24] OWEN: Sure. Starting with Betty.
[04:26] RACHEL: Okay.
[04:27] OWEN: She seems almost naive at the start, doesn't she? Full of youthful optimism.
[04:32] RACHEL: Definitely. But she doesn't stay like that for long. I think you were suggesting that she's got a lot of growing up to do. But the thing is, she does just that.
[04:42] RACHEL: She certainly grows up over the course of the novel.
[04:45] OWEN: Definitely. You can almost see her gaining confidence scene by scene.
[04:50] RACHEL: What about Sally Baxter? Not such a likable character, I found.
[04:55] OWEN: No, but she had a difficult upbringing and a lot of things go wrong for her.
[05:00] RACHEL: That's true. She's often just in the wrong place at the wrong time, through no fault of her own.
[05:06] OWEN: I know what you mean, yeah. She often seems to be a victim.
[05:10] RACHEL: Yeah, poor thing.
[05:12] OWEN: So what about the other characters? Who else is there? Oh, well, of course, there's Mrs. Dawson. What did you make of her?

[05:21] RACHEL: Well, I found it really interesting reading the dialogues involving Mrs. Dawson. She was always very perceptive and able to tell the other characters things about themselves that they hadn't realised.
[05:35] OWEN: We certainly heard plenty of wise words from her. She's an excellent problem solver. I was just sorry she didn't feature so much later in the book.
[05:44] RACHEL: And then the cook. I don't think we're ever told what her name is.
[05:48] OWEN: No, but she was quite an inspirational character. Once she made up her mind about something, she was going to get it, whatever it took.
[05:55] RACHEL: Yes, I thought her approach to life was amazing. She never let setbacks get in her way.
[06:03] OWEN: Yeah, that's right.
[06:05] RACHEL: Okay, I think we're on the right track. Shall we have a quick talk about...
[06:11] AUDIO: That is the end of part three. You now have some time to check your answers.

passages.title: SWOT analysis
content: 📌   SWOT analysis
S-W-O-T analysis may have been the idea of Albert Humphrey, who wanted to explain why [ _____ ] planning was not working.
Definition of SWOT:

S = strengths, which give a business an advantage over others.W = weaknesses, which give it a disadvantage.O = opportunities, which a business could usefully [ _____ ].T = threats, which may cause trouble.
Internal factors (strengths and weaknesses):
Examples include:what a firm sells.the price of its products or services.all the firm’s [ _____ ].the firm’s financial situation and output possibilities.
External factors (opportunities and threats):

These are usually outside a company’s control.Understanding them can reduce a company’s exposure to [ _____ ].Factors include:activities of other businesses.changes in society and fashions.new [ _____ ] that are made.what happens in the marketplace.
Uses of SWOT analysis:

For seeing what’s changing in a particular area.For reviewing a business’s strategy every [ _____ ]. [ _____ ] departments of many companies do a SWOT analysis on their principal competitors.SWOT is a useful technique not only for profit-making companies, but also for:[ _____ ].projects in the community.other non-profit groups.
Advantages of SWOT analysis:
Conducting a SWOT is [ _____ ], as anyone can do it.It improves a person’s understanding of their organisation.
Limitations of SWOT analysis:

Because an effective analysis is quick, it’s not a very detailed piece of researchIt’s based on subjective judgement, and might not be consistent.SWOT fails to take into consideration factors that might be particularly [ _____ ] in certain circumstances.
transcript: [00:02] AUDIO: Now look at part four. You will hear part of a lecture for business students about a method of analysing a business known as an SWOT or SWOT analysis. First you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40. Now listen carefully and answer questions 31 to 40.

[01:19] AUDIO: This week we are going to look at one of the oldest established frameworks for planning business strategy SWOT or SWOT analysis. Its exact origins are unclear but many attribute it to Albert Humphrey working at the Stanford Research Institute in an attempt to explain the failure of corporate planning. What is SWOT? It is an acronym for Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities and Threats.

[01:50] AUDIO: Strengths being the characteristics of a business that would put it at an advantage to its competitors, whereas the weaknesses are those that would disadvantage it. The opportunities are elements in the business environment that the business could exploit to its advantage, whereas threats are those that could cause trouble. These could then be categorised as internal and external factors. The internal factors are the characteristics of a business that are able to be ranked as strengths or weaknesses.

[02:21] AUDIO: Think about the reputation of a brand leader. This is clearly a strength when compared to a company that is just starting up and doesn't have any recognition. Other internal factors include but are not limited to what the company is selling, whether that is a product or a service, how much they are selling it for, all of the staff in the company, the organisation's finances, output possibilities and so on. Moving on to external factors.

[02:49] AUDIO: These are the areas that are beyond the company. They are out there and exist and you can't change them. However, understanding these things that are beyond your control will limit your organisation's exposure to shock and ensure that you are ready for an ever-evolving business world. These factors include what your competitors are doing, changes in society and fashions, laws being passed and trends and factors in the marketplace.

[03:17] AUDIO: So, what are the main uses for a SWOT analysis? Existing businesses can perform one at any time to check the changing environment and react accordingly. Many companies perform a SWOT analysis once a year to review strategy. New companies should also perform a SWOT analysis as part of their planning process.

[03:39] AUDIO: This would help them to better understand both the need for their product or service and how equipped they are to fit into the marketplace. Also, many marketing departments perform SWOT analyses on all their main competitors. Performing this detailed analysis is essential both for predicting upcoming challenges and also for finding out how to streamline your own business. However, it's not only profit-making companies that use a SWOT analysis.

[04:09] AUDIO: It has become a very useful organisational tool for charities, community projects and other non-profit organisations. It helps them to understand if an objective is viable and helps management to set achievable goals. So, to recap, the main benefits of conducting a SWOT analysis are that it is cheap and can be done by anybody. Secondly, it gives you a much better understanding of your company or organisation.

[04:37] AUDIO: Okay, so we've looked at the uses and benefits but there surely must be some limitations to this analysis you ask. Firstly, it can oversimplify a problem. An effective SWOT analysis is short and gets to the point and that doesn't allow for a detailed investigation. Secondly, it really is very subjective.

[05:00] AUDIO: It relies on somebody or a team of people making a judgment on what is good and bad. It is very difficult to get the same results all the time. The final and possibly most significant drawback is that all points are equally weighted in a SWOT analysis. It does not give more importance to some points that could be much more relevant to your business or its upcoming situation.

[05:25] AUDIO: So, that is a brief overview of the SWOT analysis. In our seminar later, we will be experimenting with performing an analysis on a well-known company and seeing how effective it is in practice. That is the end of part four. You now have some time to check your answers.
